findings.name: Architectural line-drawing timeline (world events below the line, firm events above)
findings.what: Full-bleed pale-grey band (#f6f6f6, ~650px tall) that scrolls sideways. One 1px grey horizontal axis at ~70% of the band height; year labels (12px sans, lining figures) interrupt the axis with small gaps ('1803–1815 —— 1815 —— 1825 —— 1850'). Under each year, a 2–4 line caption (~11px, max ~150px wide) names a WORLD event (Napoleonic wars, Geneva joins the Confederation, US financial panic). ABOVE the axis, firm milestones rise as 1px grey vertical stems of different heights, each topped by a two-line label: year in small bold sans + the street address in tracked small caps ('3, COUR SAINT-PIERRE', '26, rue de la Cité'). At the foot of each stem, standing on the axis like a street elevation, is a monochrome line drawing of the building the firm occupied. One accent stem (2px oxblood, with a dot on the axis) marks the current scrub position and carries a live counter ('5 EMPLOYEES', tracked caps). The chapter text ('1805 / THE ORIGINS OF PICTET' + paragraph) is set in oxblood at the left edge.
findings.why_valuable: Turns 'since 1805' into checkable evidence: real addresses, headcount and the crises the firm lived through. The drawn buildings are a costly, unique asset, but the language is only hairlines and small type — archival, engineer-like, unhurried. Nobody can copy it because it is made of the firm's own facts.
findings.buildable: needs-bespoke-assets — SVG line drawings of the firm's premises; axis, stems and labels are css (horizontal scroll-snap), the moving accent stem/counter is small-js. Without JS it degrades to a plain horizontally scrollable strip.
findings.three_languages: yes — labels are short and left-aligned; replace the tracked-caps address line with a lighter weight in Thai/Chinese.

findings.name: Audited key figures: figure / unit line / label / as-at footnote
findings.what: Four equal columns, each opened only by a 1px vertical rule on its left edge (no boxes, no fills). Inside each: the figure in the display serif (~56px desktop, oxblood, lining figures: '1,004', '21.9', '172', '5600+'); directly below, the unit on its own line in tracked small caps (~10px, ~0.15em: 'BN USD', 'PER CENT'); then a deliberate ~80px gap; then the metric's full name in 14px oxblood sans ending in an asterisk ('Total capital ratio*'). Under the row a body-size footnote: '*Figures as at 30 June 2026'. On phone the columns stack, each keeping its left rule.
findings.why_valuable: Reads like a note to the financial statements: unit separated from figure, metric named in full, dated as-at footnote. The asterisk discipline tells the reader the numbers are reported, not marketed — exactly the register an accounting firm should speak in.
findings.three_languages: with care — numerals survive unchanged; set the unit line in a lighter weight instead of tracked caps; Thai 'ณ วันที่ 30 มิถุนายน 2569' footnote fits.

findings.name: Press masthead plates on coverage cards
findings.what: 'In the media' row with unequal card widths (one wide ~420px + two narrow ~195px) starting at the content column; the section title 'Insights' sits alone in the left label column. Each photo is followed by a flush warm-grey plate (~40px tall, #ece8e6) carrying the publication's own masthead logotype in grey (FINANZ und WIRTSCHAFT, AGEFI FINANCE), left-aligned. Below: meta line 'Partner interview · 27 Feb 2026' (13px sans), headline in serif (~22px) written as 'Name — “quoted statement”', optional 3-line dek in sans.
findings.why_valuable: Third-party press is shown as attributed coverage — who said it, in which paper, when — instead of a logo wall. The masthead plate borrows newspaper authority while staying inside the firm's palette.
findings.three_languages: yes — mastheads are images; adapt quote marks (「」 in Chinese, “ ” in Thai).

findings.name: Audience selector as a dimmed ruled list
findings.what: Three-column band: (1) serif statement 'Select your profile to view the most relevant content' (~30px); (2) an 18px serif paragraph; (3) three audiences as rows ~75px tall separated by 1px rules, label at left, a thin → at the far right. Inactive rows are tinted to ~45% (pale rose), the hovered/active row is full oxblood with a darker arrow. No buttons, no cards, no icons.
findings.why_valuable: A door-picker for different client types that looks like an index page, not a form. The dimming makes the choice feel calm and deliberate.
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Overshooting link underline
findings.what: Text links ('Find out more', 'Learn more about the Pictet Group') in oxblood sans with a 1px rule drawn as a border, not a text underline: it sits ~4px below the baseline and runs ~12px past the last letter (inline-block + padding-right + border-bottom).
findings.why_valuable: A tiny, consistent signature: links look ruled like a ledger entry rather than browser-underlined. Costs nothing, reads as intentional.
findings.three_languages: yes — works for any script (no descender clash because the rule sits below the line box).

findings.name: Founding-year monogram replaces the wordmark on scroll
findings.what: At page top the black header carries the full condensed wordmark 'LOMBARD ODIER' with a tracked serif sub-line. After scrolling, the same 60px black header shows only a compact centred mark: a thin-line star/compass emblem with the founding year split around it — '17' left, '96' right — in ~14px serif numerals. Menu + language at left, search + account at right stay unchanged.
findings.why_valuable: The founding year rides along on every scroll position without ever being said in copy — it reads like a hallmark stamped on silver. Quiet proof of longevity.
findings.buildable: css+small-js — swap on scroll via IntersectionObserver; needs a small emblem SVG. Without JS show the full wordmark.
findings.three_languages: yes — numerals are universal; decide whether Thai shows the Buddhist-era year (e.g. 2339) or the Gregorian one.

findings.name: Centre-gutter spine (ragged-left serif meets ragged-right sans)
findings.what: Two columns meet at the page centre: the left column holds a serif statement (~30px, leading ~1.25) set flush RIGHT / ragged left; the right column holds 16px grey sans body set flush LEFT. Both text edges hug a ~30px centre gutter, so the copy forms a spine down the middle of the page. (Partly hidden by the cookie modal in the capture.)
findings.why_valuable: Feels like an open book with the gutter visible; gives a statement-then-evidence reading order and is far more considered than two left-aligned blocks.
findings.three_languages: with care — right-aligned Thai/Chinese works, but long Thai lines need a shorter measure and text-wrap: balance to avoid a jagged left edge.

findings.name: Lowercase titles closed with a full stop
findings.what: Section titles and many labels are lowercase serif with a terminal period: 'insights.', 'system changes.', 'social wall.', 'let's talk.', 'read more.' (~32px serif for titles). Tags are lowercase serif too ('investment insights', 'rethink sustainability · circular economy').
findings.why_valuable: A house voice: titles read as finished statements instead of shouted labels. Distinctive at almost zero cost.
findings.three_languages: with care — English-only device: Thai/Chinese have no case; Chinese could end with '。', Thai normally takes no full stop.

findings.name: Label sitting on the rule
findings.what: A full-width 1px grey rule closes the insights grid; a small outlined label 'discover more insights' (lowercase serif ~14px) is centred ON the rule, its background masking the line so the rule appears to pass behind it.
findings.why_valuable: Section end and 'more' action fused into one line of punctuation — quieter than a button row. (Build it square-cornered to stay off-template.)
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Staircase section composition
findings.what: Each section descends diagonally across a 12-column grid: gold tracked uppercase eyebrow (11px, ~0.2em) and a large uppercase serif title (Trirong ~60px, 3 lines, bottle green) start at col 2; the body paragraph (17px Lato, very open ~2.0 leading, grey) starts one column further in (col 3) and below the title; the photograph starts at col 6–7 with its top aligned to the paragraph's first line. Links stack vertically under the paragraph. The block steps down left → right like a staircase; the same pattern repeats for Services.
findings.why_valuable: The offset rhythm looks composed for print rather than snapped into a card grid; the eye walks title → text → image.
findings.three_languages: with care — uppercase serif titles don't exist in Thai/Chinese; keep the steps, set titles in the script's display face slightly smaller.

findings.name: South-east arrow as the house glyph
findings.what: Every link and CTA uses a gold ↘ (south-east) arrow ~14px, 8px after the label ('More about us ↘', 'View news and insights ↘', 'Contact Us ↘'). In the split hero (solid bottle-green panel + photograph of the actual banking parlour) the ↘ stands alone under the headline as the only call to action.
findings.why_valuable: The downward diagonal says 'go deeper here' rather than 'leave'; used everywhere it becomes a hallmark. Rare next to ubiquitous → and ↗.
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Crest and plumb-line section opener
findings.what: Sections open on the centre axis: the small crest (three crowns, ~30px, coral #e8553e), then 20px below a 1px coral vertical line ~120px long, then the eyebrow in sentence case (16px, plum: 'All the services you need', 'Our awards') and a centred display heading (~52px, light humanist serif, plum #3d0a1e). Used at several chapter starts, always identical.
findings.why_valuable: A heraldic punctuation mark: the brand emblem drops a thread into each chapter, like a seal on a letterhead. Calm, symmetric, unmistakably owned.
findings.three_languages: yes — eyebrow is sentence case with no tracking, so it ports directly.

findings.name: Award citation cards with square pager
findings.what: Horizontal row of tall blush cards (#f6ece8, no border, no radius, ~370×355): category top-left in small sans ('Commercial Banking', 'Digital'), the award title in display serif (~30px, plum, up to 3 lines), and the awarding body + year pinned to the bottom in small sans ('Financial Times Private Wealth Management Wealth Tech Awards 2026'). The fourth card is cut by the viewport to signal scrolling. Below: thin ← →, and SQUARE pager markers (8px squares; filled coral = current, outlined = others).
findings.why_valuable: Recognition presented as citations (award, body, year) rather than trophy logos. Square pager marks are a small, consistent departure from round template dots.
findings.buildable: css+small-js — scroll-snap row; without JS a plain horizontal scroller.
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Transactions ledger
findings.what: Full-width list, rows separated by 1px rules. Col 1 (~25% of width) holds the date only ('October 05, 2026', 14px). Cols 2–4 stack three lines: jurisdictions in small uppercase ('ITALY, LUXEMBOURG'), the transaction as a plain sentence (~24px sans), and the consideration alone on its own line ('$6.8 Billion' — or simply 'Undisclosed'). Section title in the compressed display serif; one solid CTA 'View All Transactions' under the last row, aligned to col 2.
findings.why_valuable: A register of record: dated, jurisdiction-tagged, with 'Undisclosed' stated openly — precision and discretion in the same line. No logos, no cards. An accounting firm can run the same ledger with anonymised engagements ('Listed manufacturer · TFRS 16 transition · Undisclosed').
findings.three_languages: yes — don't rely on uppercase for the jurisdiction line; use local date formats.

findings.name: Report cover as a typographic tile
findings.what: The featured research item is a flat grey-blue panel (~900×600) treated as a printed cover: a 1px vertical rule inset ~25px from the left edge, the title set large in classical serif (~60px) in TWO tones — series title in pale blue ('The New Supply-Side Era:'), issue title in white ('The O-Ring Meets Geopolitics') — and a 1px horizontal rule near the foot with the firm name below. To its left, a narrow column of three items: category in small caps, blue title, a long thin → on its own line, rules between.
findings.why_valuable: Thought leadership looks like a paper the firm actually published — no stock image needed, and the two-tone title separates series from issue.
findings.three_languages: yes — pure type; pair with a Thai/Chinese serif (e.g. Noto Serif Thai / Noto Serif SC).

findings.name: Tight-set compressed display serif
findings.what: Headings in VC Garamond at large sizes (96px hero, ~60px sections) with negative tracking (~-0.03em) and leading ~1.0, letters nearly touching; body and UI in Helvetica Neue regular; links in a single corporate blue, each followed by a long thin → (~30px) on its own line.
findings.why_valuable: The squeezed serif has newspaper confidence; paired with neutral Helvetica it reads as an old institution that still edits tightly.
findings.buildable: css (licensed serif with a condensed cut)
findings.three_languages: with care — negative tracking must be off for Thai (stacked vowels/tone marks collide) and Chinese.

findings.name: Archival engraving among photographs
findings.what: In a three-up 'Learn More' row of equal tiles (~435×245), the 'History' tile is a monochrome ink drawing of the original 'S. LAZARD & CO.' storefront, at the same size and crop as the two contemporary colour photographs beside it; identical blue label + arrow below each.
findings.why_valuable: One archival image among modern photos does the heritage work silently — no 'Est. 1848' badge needed.
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Tombstone panel with units declared '(VALUES IN MILLIONS)'
findings.what: Half-width light-grey panel: label 'FEATURED TRANSACTIONS' in small bold caps, with a second line in italic caps '(VALUES IN MILLIONS)'. Then the role verb 'Advising' (18px), the client logo, the deal as a sentence ('on its sale to Apollo'), and a closing line 'Lead Financial Advisor  |  ~£5,700' — role and approximate value split by a vertical bar. Paginated by a long row of 17 small dots + 'VIEW ALL'.
findings.why_valuable: The parenthetical unit declaration is lifted straight from financial-statement headers, and the tilde admits approximation — numeracy and honesty at a glance. It is the exact convention accountants use, which makes it fit perfectly.
findings.buildable: css+small-js — slider; without JS render as a vertical list.
findings.three_languages: with care — the unit note ports perfectly (Thai '(หน่วย: ล้านบาท)' is the standard Thai statement header), but drop italics and caps.

findings.name: Hairline condensed numerals with approximation marks
findings.what: Key figures in an ultra-condensed light sans (Giorgio Sans), ~90px, white on dark navy, in a 2×2 grid; label below each in 16px light-blue sans ('Current Employees', 'Year Founded', 'Countries with Evercore Offices', 'Announced Transactions'). Approximate values carry a small tilde ('~2,600'); cumulative ones a plus ('$5T+').
findings.why_valuable: Tall, thin numerals look engraved and exact rather than loud; the tilde and plus are honest qualifiers.
findings.three_languages: yes — numerals universal, labels short.

findings.name: Engraved line-field background
findings.what: Dark navy panels (~#0b2545) filled with thousands of fine parallel curved lines (~1px, 3–4px pitch, very low contrast) bending in broad waves like banknote guilloché or a contour map; used behind the stats and the news column. These textured halves alternate with plain white/grey text halves in a 720px checkerboard.
findings.why_valuable: Fine-line engraving is the visual language of banknotes and share certificates — security and value — and gives depth without a photograph.
findings.buildable: css — generated SVG pattern as background; degrades to flat navy.
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Office directory naming the legal entity per office
findings.what: Footer right half lists offices as blocks: city (16px), then in 11px grey the registered entity for that office ('Centerview Partners UK LLP', 'Centerview Partners France SCS'), street, floor, city + postcode; a second column aligned to the first line carries the numbers with trailing labels ('(212) 380-2650 | Tel', '… | Fax'). Below: 'Copyright © 2008 - 2026 Centerview Partners Holdings LP' and 'member SIPC'.
findings.why_valuable: Naming the registered entity per office is what regulators and careful clients look for — real, licensed presence rather than a pin on a map.
findings.three_languages: yes — Thai version would add company registration / tax ID per office.

findings.name: Mechanism diagrams instead of service icons
findings.what: Six services in one row, each above its label: a ~110px line diagram in 1px grey-violet strokes that shows how the service works — two overlapping circles with converging arrows (M&A), a '$' circle over dashed circles (capital raising), a parent circle branching to three (restructuring), three circles orbited by arrows (special committee), a person circle radiating to dashed circles (shareholder engagement), nodes joined by right-angle arrows (private funds). Solid vs dashed strokes distinguish parties. The selected service is marked by a small chevron beneath, and its description spans the full width below the row.
findings.why_valuable: Each drawing explains the mechanism like a partner's whiteboard sketch — precise, schematic and owned — instead of generic stock icons.
findings.buildable: needs-bespoke-assets — a set of SVG line diagrams (for accountants: consolidation, audit trail, VAT flow, payroll cycle); tabs are small-js, without JS all descriptions show.
findings.three_languages: yes — labels sit under the drawings.

findings.name: Brand slash as layout divider
findings.what: The logotype 'P / W / P' uses thin slanted slashes; the same slash reappears as a 1px diagonal hairline (~120px tall, ~10° off vertical) separating a section heading ('Join Our Team', 52px light sans, left) from its paragraph and underlined caps link (right).
findings.why_valuable: One mark from the logo becomes the layout's punctuation — an identity system, not decoration.
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Value-first tombstone wall
findings.what: Four-column grid without boxes, only 1px vertical rules between columns. Each cell: client logo in ~50% grey, the deal value (~22px: '~$3B', '£2.3B', '$20B+'), and the role as a centred 15px grey sentence ('Lead financial advisor to Thorne on its sale to Procter & Gamble'). 'VIEW MORE' underlined caps after eight cells.
findings.why_valuable: Greyscale logos stay subordinate to the number and the role; ~ and + keep the figures truthful.
findings.three_languages: yes — but accountants usually need an anonymised version (sector instead of logo).

findings.name: Entity-by-jurisdiction regulatory footer
findings.what: Grey footer: an underlined caps sitemap row, then one plain paragraph per jurisdiction ('Investment banking services in the United Kingdom are offered through Perella Weinberg UK Limited (“PWP-UK”), which is authorized and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority.'), every regulator name linked; then greyscale regulator badges (CIRO, CIPF MEMBER) and links to disclosures.
findings.why_valuable: Plain-language disclosure of who does what under which licence — trust built from facts. For a Thai accounting firm: licensed auditor numbers, DBD registration, TFAC membership.
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Notched frame system
findings.what: Containers are drawn with 1px lines that deliberately don't close: the top edge starts ~30px in from the top-left corner and the bottom edge stops ~30px short of the bottom-right corner, while both sides run full height. The same notched outline is used for insight cards (white on navy), AUM boxes (purple on white) and even the outline button ('LEARN ABOUT KKR'). Cards inset the image by 16px, then bold caps category, light-sans title, caps date.
findings.why_valuable: One consistent line rule across every container makes the system recognisable and slightly architectural, like drafting brackets — off the generic card look without adding colour.
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Raised currency sign and as-of note
findings.what: Four notched boxes in a row; each figure has '$' set small (~40% size) and raised to cap height at the left of the number, the value in light sans (~48px, '255B'), then the asset class in small tracked caps ('PRIVATE EQUITY'). Under the row a single line: 'As of June 30, 2026. Credit AUM including liquid strategies is $331B.'
findings.why_valuable: The raised currency sign is a financial-table typesetting habit; the as-of note with its exception clause reads like a reconciliation.
findings.three_languages: yes — ฿/¥ raise the same way; replace tracked caps in Thai/Chinese.

findings.name: Anniversary numeral lockup
findings.what: The sans wordmark 'KKR' is followed by a 1px vertical hairline and the anniversary numeral '50' in a calligraphic serif, same purple, slightly taller than the caps; the hero headline repeats '50 years of partnership' with a short blue rule beneath.
findings.why_valuable: Marks a milestone inside the logo for one season without redesigning the brand; the contrasting serif numeral works like a date stamp.
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Felt-pen annotation on a single word
findings.what: A one-line serif statement ('We help the daring build legendary companies.', ~48px, centred, large white field) carries a hand-drawn green marker stroke: a loose ellipse around 'daring' whose tail continues as an underline under 'help the'. The device recurs at the end of a litany panel (eight one-sentence lines in serif on mustard, closing with 'These are our people.' and 'people' circled). Strokes have uneven width and overshoot like a real felt pen.
findings.why_valuable: A human editorial gesture on otherwise strict type — someone read and marked this sentence. For an accounting firm it maps directly onto the reviewer's tick-and-circle mark on working papers.
findings.buildable: css+small-js — inline SVG path drawn on with stroke-dashoffset; static SVG without JS.
findings.three_languages: with care — wrap the target term in a span so the stroke can be positioned (Chinese has no word spaces); size the ellipse per script.

findings.name: Motion ON / OFF switch in the footer
findings.what: In the footer's right column a labelled control 'MOTION' with two outlined pill toggles 'ON' and 'OFF' (active = brighter outline), sitting above the copyright line.
findings.why_valuable: Gives visitors explicit control over animation, beyond the OS reduced-motion setting — considerate, accessible, and almost never offered.
findings.buildable: css+small-js — toggle a class on <html>, persist in localStorage; without JS honour prefers-reduced-motion.
findings.three_languages: yes — two short words.

findings.name: Rails and rules framework
findings.what: Content sits between full-height 1px vertical rails at the outer content edges plus one rail between the two columns; each card has a short 1px horizontal rule (inset to the card width) ~16px above and below it, like a contact sheet. Navigation in tiny monospace caps ('OUR FOUNDERS', 'OUR COMPANIES'); card type in monospace caps with a small glyph top-left ('● PODCAST', 'SPOTLIGHT') and the verb top-right ('LISTEN', 'READ').
findings.why_valuable: A drafting-table framework visible behind the content gives order and editorial confidence; monospace labels add archival precision.
findings.three_languages: with care — monospace caps labels must switch to the script's UI face.

findings.name: The firm's name as the whole statement
findings.what: Hero: full-screen duotone navy photograph of a façade with only the firm name centred in letterspaced small caps (~28px, white) and a thin chevron below — no tagline, no button, no logo in the header. The footer repeats it as a colophon: name in grey small caps centred, a ~60px centred hairline, a one-line address, then 't. 212.403.1000 or 800.848.0301 / Attorney Advertising and Other Notices'. No sitemap, no social icons.
findings.why_valuable: Extreme restraint: the name is assumed to be enough, and that assumption is the claim. The footer reads like the last page of a book.
findings.three_languages: with care — no small caps in Thai/Chinese; set the name in its script at a lighter weight, letter-spacing 0.

findings.name: Italic publication titles inside headlines
findings.what: News headlines in Playfair Display (~30px) put publication names in true italics, as in printed editorial style: '15 Attorneys Named to *Lawdragon*'s List…', '*Lexology Index*: Thought Leaders USA 2027', '*Forbes*' 2026 List'.
findings.why_valuable: Correct bibliographic convention signals literacy and editorial care that most corporate CMS headlines lose.
findings.three_languages: with care — Thai has no italics (use quotation marks); Chinese uses 《 》 for titles; the builder should map <cite> per language.

findings.name: Zebra columns under a label bar
findings.what: Each content row is a full-bleed four-column band whose columns alternate two very pale blue-grey tints (#e8edf4 / #f2f5f9) — no gaps, borders or shadows. The row is headed by a full-width bar in a slightly darker tint: label at left ('RECENT REPRESENTATIONS', 13px caps) and a solid blue 'VIEW MORE ›' tab flush right. Headlines in light serif (~30px) describe matters as phrases ('TowneBank in its $154 million acquisition of blueharbor bank').
findings.why_valuable: Ledger-like banding: separation by tone alone, like a printed table with alternate shading.
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Echo headline (the headline is its own background)
findings.what: Feature hero on a pale-blue field: the deal headline centred in a Bembo-like serif (~52px, navy, 4 lines) under a tracked eyebrow 'DEALS & CASES' and a short vertical tick; behind it the same words repeat at ~250px in pale blue, cropped by the frame on all sides; a soft radial white glow sits behind the readable text to separate the two layers. Small → below.
findings.why_valuable: The text becomes its own image — no photograph, no stock — and the scale contrast gives a single deal the weight of a poster.
findings.buildable: css (pure type; optional slow drift with small-js)
findings.three_languages: with care — works with Thai/Chinese glyphs, but echo only a short key phrase so cropping stays legible.

findings.name: Hanging heading with section numeral
findings.what: Homepage sections are numbered '01', '02', '03' in small grey lining numerals set above the heading and aligned to the BODY indent; the heading (~52px serif) hangs ~80px to the left of the body column; body in a large book serif (~28px, leading ~1.6, ~65 characters per line); link 'EXPLORE →' in tracked small caps.
findings.why_valuable: Classic book typography — outdented heads and numbered chapters — makes the homepage read like a bound brief.
findings.three_languages: yes — numerals universal; replace the tracked-caps link in Thai/Chinese.

findings.name: Headline-only news carousel
findings.what: News slider with no images: each slide is a 1px rule then a large serif headline (~48px, 3–4 lines, ~630px wide); neighbouring slides peek in at both edges at ~35% opacity, cut by the viewport, some in italic; centred '‹ 1/6 ›' counter below.
findings.why_valuable: News presented as typeset text with authority instead of stock photos — cheaper to maintain and more distinguished.
findings.buildable: css+small-js — scroll-snap; without JS a horizontal scroller.
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Expanding matter tiles
findings.what: 'Recent work' row of four tall outlined tiles (1px purple border, square corners, ~225×380): date top-left ('05 October 2026', 16px) and a short matter description bottom-left in 13px. The active tile (hover/focus — one was expanded in frame 03, none in frame 04) widens to ~2× and fills solid purple, its description promoted to a white serif headline (~28px). Outline button 'View all recent work' below.
findings.why_valuable: Dated matters as an index of quiet tiles — no logos, no photos — opened one at a time like pulling a file. Proves activity while staying discreet.
findings.buildable: css (flex-grow on :hover/:focus-within) + small-js for keyboard/auto-advance; without JS all tiles stay equal and readable.
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Open rounded bracket frame
findings.what: Major blocks are enclosed by a single 1px line running along the TOP and down the LEFT side only, joined by a ~24px radius at the top-left corner; the top line runs off the right edge, the left line stops where the block ends — an open file-tab bracket. The hero puts a two-line serif statement (~80px) and a sans dek at bottom-left inside the bracket under a large empty field; the footer reuses the same bracket in white on black around each group of links.
findings.why_valuable: A box becomes the edge of a document or folder — editorial and architectural, consistent from hero to footer, achieved with one line.
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Two-question qualifier
findings.what: Beside a photograph: 'Answer two questions and put our thinking to work on your challenges.' then '1. What is your industry?' in bold with a grey 'Question 1 of 2' counter, followed by a wrap of choice chips (outlined, red text; selected = solid red) and a 'View all' link; step 2 then narrows to tailored content.
findings.why_valuable: A tailored entry like a partner's first-meeting questions, explicit about the effort asked (two questions). Shortens the path for a firm with many service lines without a chatbot.
findings.buildable: css+small-js — radio groups; without JS the chips are links to industry pages. Use square chips to stay off-template.
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Case story closed by impact figures
findings.what: Label 'Featured client success story' over a 1px rule, case title (~40px bold sans), then 'The impact' and 2–3 grey square tiles (#efefef, ~220×195), each a large numeral (~40px: '500+', '7') with the unit spelled out as a phrase beneath ('months from ideation to launch'). 'Read story ▸' in red; image to the right.
findings.why_valuable: Every case ends in quantified outcomes — evidence instead of adjectives.
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Save-for-later library
findings.what: A bookmark ribbon icon at the bottom-right of each insight card (next to its content type: 'Brief', 'Technology Report'), a bookmark in the main header and a 'SAVED ITEMS' folder menu in the utility bar.
findings.why_valuable: Treats the knowledge section as a library the reader builds — signals depth and invites return visits.
findings.buildable: css+small-js — localStorage; without JS hide the icons.
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Metric-led case tiles
findings.what: Carousel of client stories: each photo tile has a translucent chip in its top-left corner with the outcome number (~28px: '$4.5b+') and a two-line caps unit ('IN BOTTOM-LINE IMPACT DELIVERED', 'TRADE PRODUCTS', 'PRODUCTIVITY'); a translucent panel at the bottom carries 'CLIENT IMPACT' and the story title; the first tile is wider and shows the summary + CTA.
findings.why_valuable: The outcome number is the first thing read on each case, with its unit spelled out. (Frosted-glass styling itself is template-like.)
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Matted photograph on an artwork field
findings.what: Half-width panel filled edge-to-edge with an abstract artwork (golden folds); a documentary photograph sits centred on it inside a thick white mat (~26px, square corners), like a framed print hung on a wall.
findings.why_valuable: Gallery mounting gives an ordinary staff photo the dignity of a print and lets brand art and real photography coexist.
findings.buildable: css (padding + background); the artwork field needs-bespoke-assets
findings.three_languages: yes

findings.name: Spotlight topic bar in the header
findings.what: Floating header in three detached white blocks with a soft shadow: menu + logo left, search + login right, and a centre block 'BCG SPOTLIGHT' (small caps label) followed by three underlined topic links ('ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE', 'CEO AGENDA', 'COST MANAGEMENT').
findings.why_valuable: Curated current topics in the header show the firm is on top of the moment — editorial and changeable each season (e.g. 'Spotlight: half-year CIT filing · e-Tax Invoice · TFRS for NPAEs').
findings.three_languages: yes

site_notes.pictet.com: Lardy Serif for headings/statements + Lardy Sans for UI and captions; about five sizes (≈56/30/22/16/12, ratio ≈1.33). One oxblood accent for links, figures and active states on white/off-white. Grid: a ~30% left label column with section names, content in the right 70% (often 2 sub-columns). Sections separated by full-bleed 1px rules and one grey band. GSAP + WebGL detected; the video hero did not render in the capture (blank area under the headline).
site_notes.lombardodier.com: PARTIAL: a large cookie modal covers the centre of every desktop and phone frame; findings come from the visible margins. Custom Lombard Odier serif (Palatino-like) + Helvetica Neue; black header; lowercase serif voice; dark 'why us' band with '+195 / +24 / +215' figures and vertical hairline separators.
site_notes.hoaresbank.co.uk: Trirong uppercase serif headings + Lato body; bottle green #0f3a33, gold accent, linen #f8f6f1 bands. Split hero (solid green panel ~44% + photograph of the real banking parlour, vertical 'SCROLL' + social rail). Content series 'Alexander's Letters' (a partner's letters) as an insight category. Carousel with a gold progress line.
site_notes.juliusbaer.com_en: FAILED: a geo-redirect modal ('Welcome to Julius Baer's international site', plus cookie choices on phone) covers every frame and the page never scrolled. Nothing reviewable.
site_notes.coutts.com: Coutts Siena (light humanist display) + Coutts Forme; plum #3d0a1e, coral accent, blush #f6ece8. Centred, symmetric chapters opened by crest + plumb line; square-cornered outline buttons; full-bleed abstract paintings behind a white panel for 'Our history'. Columns divided by thin coral rules that turn horizontal on phone.
site_notes.lazard.com: VC Garamond compressed, tight-tracked headings + Helvetica Neue body; navy text, one corporate blue for links, warm-grey band (#ebe7e0) for news. A recurring 25% date column (transactions, news) gives the page the consistency of a register. Long thin arrows on their own line under every link.
site_notes.evercore.com: IBM Plex Sans light for headings and body (the serif lives only in the wordmark), Giorgio Sans for figures; navy, white, light grey. Page assembled from 720px half-tiles in a checkerboard; engraved line-field texture on navy halves; outlined square buttons.
site_notes.centerviewpartners.com: Dated template build (Nunito Sans, B&W architecture photography, checkerboard service tiles, inline 'Read More' micro-pills). Only the office directory is distinctive.
site_notes.pwpartners.com: Work Sans light (≈60px headings) + Inter-like body; monochrome violet-grey; painterly brush-stroke hero art with a circular hairline text button; slashes from the P/W/P logotype reused as dividers; tombstone wall of deal values.
site_notes.kkr.com: Ghost (light humanist sans) up to 132px; purple, navy, yellow. Notched 1px outlines on every container; fine-line ribbon '&' illustration; anniversary lockup 'KKR | 50'. Hero video failed in the capture (error overlay).
site_notes.sequoiacap.com: Rosart (serif statements) + Pitch Sans (monospace UI caps) + Unica77; cream #f9f6f0 page, rails-and-rules framework, flat bold panels (green, mustard, blue, black) with white hand-drawn illustrations; Lenis smooth scroll; felt-pen annotations; user-facing motion switch.
site_notes.wlrk.com: PARTIAL: only three desktop frames (short page). Playfair Display headlines + Arial/Helvetica UI; slate-blue duotone; translucent slate header bar overlaying content; name-only hero and colophon footer; zebra-tinted columns.
site_notes.cravath.com: Bembo (headings and long body) + Franklin Gothic ITC (tracked small-caps UI); navy + pale blue; numbered chapters with hanging heads; echo-type hero; dark 'Bicentennial' band with diagonal light streaks. A cookie bar covers the lower ~25% of every frame.
site_notes.slaughterandmay.com: Feature Deck serif (purple) + Open Sans; one italic accent word in the hero ('Our *expertise* in practice'); lavender band for insights; typographic tiles with label top / title bottom and no image; expanding matter tiles.
site_notes.freshfields.com: FreshfieldsHeadline serif + FreshfieldsText sans; cream #f9f7ee, black, periwinkle accents; open rounded brackets as the container system; risograph-like commissioned illustrations; edge-to-edge extended-sans wordmark in the footer (common on agency sites, not recorded as a finding).
site_notes.bain.com: Graphik + Tiempos (serif for card deks); red, black, white; Barba page transitions; hero story switcher with a short red dash over the active tab; hero/video error overlay in the capture.
site_notes.bcg.com: henderson-bcg serif headings + sans; dark green, bright green pill CTAs and rounded floating header blocks (template-leaning). Only the matted print, spotlight bar and metric chips are worth keeping.
